I have been farming this same land for over 40 years. My husband still helps when his back allows, but mostly it is me now. Our sons work in the city — they send money sometimes, but the land is mine to manage. We have about 8 mu of flatland.

I will do what I have always done, what my mother did, what every family here does: winter wheat, then summer corn. That is the only way to use the land twice in one year and have enough income. I have never tried anything else, and at my age I am not going to gamble on something unfamiliar.

For wheat, I will buy seed from the village supply shop — the same improved variety I bought last year, Kenong 199 or whatever they have in stock that others say is good. I do not read the bags carefully, I ask the shop owner. I will apply compound fertilizer as a base before planting, then spread urea at jointing stage. I put a little more than they say because I cannot afford a thin harvest. I will irrigate four times: once before sowing to prepare the seedbed, once in early spring after the freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. I will spray for aphids and powdery mildew twice.

For corn, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. The machine does most of it now. I buy hybrid seed — Xianyu or Zhengdan, whatever is at the shop. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. Summer rains usually help, so I only need to pump water once or twice if it is dry. I spray once for stem borer.

I do not grow vegetables this year — my knees are bad and the vegetable market price has been low.
